The wording could include all believers from every nation, but the expression "inheriting the Book" applied only to the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, and the earlier ones did not inherit it. It was also said: the chosen ones are the Prophets, who inherited the Book in the sense that it passed from some of them to others. Allah said: ﴿And Solomon inherited David﴾ [al-Naml: 16], and He said: ﴿He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾ [Maryam: 6]. If prophethood can be inherited, then the Book can likewise be inherited. ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ refers to whoever has fallen into a minor sin. Ibn Atiyya said: This view is rejected on several grounds. Al-Dahhak said: The meaning of ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ is: among their descendants is one who wrongs himself, and he is the polytheist. Al-Hasan said: from among their nations, according to what has been mentioned earlier of the disagreement concerning the wrongdoer. The verse concerns the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ.

The expressions of the people of the hearts (arbab al-qulub, the Sufis) have varied concerning the wrongdoer, the moderate and the foremost. Sahl ibn Abd Allah said: the foremost is the scholar, the moderate is the learner, and the wrongdoer is the ignorant. Dhu'l-Nun al-Misri said: the wrongdoer is the one who remembers Allah with his tongue only, the moderate is the one who remembers Him with his heart, and the foremost is the one who never forgets Him. Al-Antaki said: the wrongdoer is the possessor of words, the moderate is the possessor of deeds, and the foremost is the possessor of spiritual states. Ibn Ata said: the wrongdoer is the one who loves Allah for the sake of this world, the moderate is the one who loves Him for the sake of the reward in the Hereafter, and the foremost is the one who has dropped his own desire in favour of the desire of the Real. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who worships Allah out of fear of the Fire, the moderate is the one who worships Allah out of hope for Paradise, and the foremost is the one who worships Allah for His own sake, without any cause. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who renounces the world, because he has wronged himself by forsaking for it a share, which is knowledge and love; the moderate is the one who knows (al-'arif), and the foremost is the one who loves (al-muhibb). It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who becomes distressed at trial, the moderate is the one who is patient under trial, and the foremost is the one who takes pleasure in trial. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who worships Allah in heedlessness and by habit, the moderate is the one who worships Him out of desire and dread, and the foremost is the one who worships Him out of awe. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who is given and withholds, the moderate is the one who is given and gives, and the foremost is the one who is denied and gives thanks and prefers others. It is related that two devout worshippers met, and one said: "How are your brothers in Basra?" He replied: "Well: if they are given, they give thanks, and if they are denied, they are patient." The other said: "This is the condition of dogs with us in Balkh! Our worshippers, if they are denied, give thanks, and if they are given, they prefer others." It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who is self-sufficient through his wealth, the moderate is the one who is self-sufficient through his religion, and the foremost is the one who is self-sufficient through his Lord. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who recites the Qur'an but does not act by it, the moderate is the one who recites the Qur'an and acts by it, and the foremost is the reciter of the Qur'an who acts by it and knows it. It was also said: the foremost is the one who enters the mosque before the muezzin's call to prayer (adhan), the moderate is the one who enters the mosque after the adhan has been called, and the wrongdoer is the one who enters the mosque when the prayer has already been established (iqamah), because he has wronged himself of the reward and has not obtained for himself what others obtained. Some people of knowledge said regarding this: rather, the foremost is the one who attains both the time and the congregation, and thus attains both virtues; the moderate is the one who, if the congregation is missed, does not neglect the time; and the wrongdoer is the one heedless of the prayer until both the time and the congregation are missed, so he is more deserving of the designation of wrongdoing. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who loves himself, the moderate is the one who loves his religion, and the foremost is the one who loves his Lord. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who takes his due but does not give what is due, the moderate is the one who takes his due and gives what is due, and the foremost is the one who gives what is due and does not take his due.

A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The foremost is the one who embraced Islam before the Hijrah, the moderate is the one who embraced Islam after the Hijrah, and the wrongdoer is the one who did not embrace Islam except under the sword, and all of them are forgiven. I say: al-Tha'labi mentioned these views and more in his Tafsir. In sum, they are two extremes and a middle, and the moderate (al-muqtasid) is the one who holds firmly to the course (al-qasd), which is the avoidance of inclination. From this is the saying of Jabir ibn Hunayy al-Tha'labi:

*We grant the kings peace as long as they keep to the course with us,*
*and killing them is not forbidden to us.*

That is, we offer them reconciliation as long as they ride the course with us, that is, as long as they do not oppress; and killing them is not forbidden to us if they transgress. Therefore the moderate holds a station between the two stations: he is above the one who wrongs himself and below the one who is foremost in good deeds.

﴿That is the great bounty﴾ means Our bringing them the Book. It was also said: that choosing, with Our knowledge of their faults, is the great bounty. It was also said: the promise of Paradise to these three categories is a great bounty.

**The third:** People have discussed placing the wrongdoer before the moderate and the foremost. It was said: mention first does not imply honour, as in His saying: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal﴾ [al-Hashr: 20]. It was also said: the wrongdoer is placed first because of the abundance of sinners among them and their dominance, while the moderate are few in comparison to them, and the foremost are fewer than the few. This was mentioned by al-Zamakhshari, and no one else mentioned it. It was also said: the wrongdoer is placed first to emphasise hope on his behalf, since he has nothing to rely upon except the mercy of his Lord; the moderate relies on his good opinion, and the foremost relies on his obedience. It was also said: the wrongdoer is placed first so that he does not despair of the mercy of Allah, and the foremost is placed last so that he does not become conceited by his deed. Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sadiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The wrongdoer is placed first to inform that one can only draw near to Him through the bestowal of His mercy and generosity, and that wrongdoing does not affect the choosing when there is care from Him. Then He mentions the moderate in the second place, because they are between fear and hope. Then He concludes with the foremost, so that no one feels secure from the plotting of Allah. And all of them are in Paradise through the sanctity of the word of sincerity: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi said: He gathered them in the choosing, removing the causes from the giving, because choosing necessitates inheritance, not inheritance necessitating choosing. For this reason it is said in the wisdom literature: "Correct the lineage, then claim the inheritance." It was also said: He placed the foremost last so that they would be nearer to the gardens and the reward, just as He placed the monasteries and churches before the mosques in Surah al-Hajj, so that the monasteries would be nearer to destruction and ruin, and the mosques nearer to the remembrance of Allah. It was also said: when kings wish to join things in mention, they put the nearer first, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in retribution, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-A'raf: 167], and His saying: ﴿He bestows female offspring on whom He wills and bestows males on whom He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 49], and His saying: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal﴾ [al-Hashr: 20]. I say: How well has the one said who said:

And the ultimate of this generosity is you, but it [only] reaches the ends at the last of matters.

Fourth issue: His saying, "Gardens of Eden they will enter" (*jannatu 'adnin yadkhulunaha*). He grouped them together in the entering because it is an inheritance, and the disobedient and the dutiful are equal in an inheritance when they both acknowledge the lineage. So the disobedient and the obedient are both joined to the Lord.

It was also read as *"Jannatu 'adnin"* in the singular, as if it were a garden specific to the foremost (*al-sabiqun*) because of their fewness, as has been mentioned previously. And *"Jannati 'adnin"* in the accusative is by an implied verb (*idmar*) that the apparent verb explains, meaning: they enter the gardens of Eden, they enter them. This applies to all of them, and it is the correct view, God willing, Exalted is He.

Abu 'Amr read *yudkhaluna-ha* with a *damma* on the *ya'* and a *fatha* on the *kha'*, and he said it is based on His saying, "They will be adorned [therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein is silk]" [[See vol. 12, p. 28.]].

"And they will say, 'Praise be to God, who has removed from us all grief.'" Abu Thabit said: A man entered the mosque and said, "O God, have mercy on my estrangement, console my loneliness, and facilitate for me a righteous companion." Abu al-Darda' said: "If you are truthful, then I am happier with that than you are. I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants; of them is one who wrongs himself, and of them is one who is moderate, and of them is one who is foremost in good deeds'" [Qur'an 35:32] — he said: "This foremost one comes and enters Paradise without reckoning; as for the moderate one, he is reckoned with an easy reckoning; and as for the one who wrongs himself, he is detained in the place of standing, rebuked and reproached, and then he enters Paradise. They are the ones who say, 'Praise be to God, who has removed from us all grief; indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative'" [Qur'an 35:34].

In another wording: "As for those who wronged themselves, they will be detained for a long time on the Day of Gathering, and then it is they whom God meets with His mercy. They are the ones who say, 'Praise be to God, who has removed from us all grief; indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative,' up to His saying, 'and no fatigue will touch us therein'" [Qur'an 35:35].

It was also said: "He is the one who is taken to account in his station," meaning that he is expiated for what afflicts him of distress and grief. From this is His saying: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ [Qur'an 4:123], meaning in this world. Al-Tha'labi said: "This interpretation is more fitting to the apparent meaning, because He said, 'Gardens of Eden they will enter,' and because of His saying, 'those whom We chose from among Our servants,' and the disbeliever and the hypocrite were not chosen."

I say: This is the correct view. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The likeness of the hypocrite who recites the Qur'an is like the sweet basil: its scent is pleasant, but its taste is bitter." So he informed that the hypocrite recites it, while the Exalted and Glorified God informed that the hypocrite is in the lowest depth of the Fire. Many disbelievers, Jews, and Christians also recite it in our time.

Malik said: "Someone who has no good in him may recite the Qur'an."

*Al-nasab*: fatigue. *Al-lughub*: exhaustion.

According to this view, the object of the verb of choosing in His saying, ﴿We have given the Book to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾, is considered to be an omitted genitive (mudaf) construction, as the omitted mudaf occurs in ﴿And ask the town﴾ [Yusuf: 82], meaning: We chose their religion. Then what remains is "We chose them," so the returning pronoun to the relative clause (al-'a'id ila'l-mawsul) is omitted, as it is omitted in His saying, ﴿And I do not say to those whom your eyes look down upon﴾ [Hud: 31], meaning: whom your eyes look down upon. Thus the choosing is directed to their religion, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has chosen for you the religion﴾ [al-Baqarah: 132]. Al-Nahhas said: There is a third view: the wrongdoer is the one who commits major sins, and the moderate is the one who does not deserve Paradise by having his good deeds outweigh his bad deeds. Thus ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, they will enter them﴾ applies only to those who were foremost in good deeds. This is the view of a group of people of reflection, because in the strict sense of reasoning the pronoun should refer to what is nearest to it. I say: The middle view is the best and the most sound, if Allah wills, because the disbeliever and the hypocrite were not chosen, praise be to Allah, and their religion was not chosen. This is the view of six of the Companions, and that is sufficient for you. We shall elaborate and clarify it further in the rest of the verse.

**The second:** His saying, ﴿We have given the Book﴾, meaning We gave. Inheritance (al-mirath) is a gift, in reality or metaphorically, since it is said of what comes to a person after another's death. Here "the Book" is meant to include the meanings of the Book, its knowledge, its rulings and its creed. It is as though Allah, when He gave the Qur'an to the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, and it included the meanings of the revealed Books, He thereby bequeathed to the Ummah of Muhammad, peace be upon him, the Book that was among the nations before us.

(Isṭafaynā) means We chose. Its derivation is from ṣafw, which is purity, freedom from the impurities of turbidity. Its original form is iṣtafawnā, then the tā' was changed to ṭā' and the wāw to yā'.

(Min ʿibādinā) It was said that what is meant is the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, as said by Ibn Abbas and others. The wording could include all believers from every nation, but the expression "inheriting the Book" applied only to the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, and the earlier ones did not inherit it. It was also said: the chosen ones are the Prophets, who inherited the Book in the sense that it passed from some of them to others. Allah said: ﴿And Solomon inherited David﴾ [al-Naml: 16], and He said: ﴿He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾ [Maryam: 6]. If prophethood can be inherited, then the Book can likewise be inherited. ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ refers to whoever has fallen into a minor sin. Ibn Atiyya said: This view is rejected on several grounds. Al-Dahhak said: The meaning of ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ is: among their descendants is one who wrongs himself, and he is the polytheist. Al-Hasan said: from among their nations, according to what has been mentioned earlier of the disagreement concerning the wrongdoer. The verse concerns the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ.

The expressions of the people of the hearts (arbab al-qulub, the Sufis) have varied concerning the wrongdoer, the moderate and the foremost. Sahl ibn Abd Allah said: the foremost is the scholar, the moderate is the learner, and the wrongdoer is the ignorant. Dhu'l-Nun al-Misri said: the wrongdoer is the one who remembers Allah with his tongue only, the moderate is the one who remembers Him with his heart, and the foremost is the one who never forgets Him. Al-Antaki said: the wrongdoer is the possessor of words, the moderate is the possessor of deeds, and the foremost is the possessor of spiritual states. Ibn Ata said: the wrongdoer is the one who loves Allah for the sake of this world, the moderate is the one who loves Him for the sake of the reward in the Hereafter, and the foremost is the one who has dropped his own desire in favour of the desire of the Real. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who worships Allah out of fear of the Fire, the moderate is the one who worships Allah out of hope for Paradise, and the foremost is the one who worships Allah for His own sake, without any cause. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who renounces the world, because he has wronged himself by forsaking for it a share, which is knowledge and love; the moderate is the one who knows (al-'arif), and the foremost is the one who loves (al-muhibb). It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who becomes distressed at trial, the moderate is the one who is patient under trial, and the foremost is the one who takes pleasure in trial. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who worships Allah in heedlessness and by habit, the moderate is the one who worships Him out of desire and dread, and the foremost is the one who worships Him out of awe. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who is given and withholds, the moderate is the one who is given and gives, and the foremost is the one who is denied and gives thanks and prefers others. It is related that two devout worshippers met, and one said: "How are your brothers in Basra?" He replied: "Well: if they are given, they give thanks, and if they are denied, they are patient." The other said: "This is the condition of dogs with us in Balkh! Our worshippers, if they are denied, give thanks, and if they are given, they prefer others." It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who is self-sufficient through his wealth, the moderate is the one who is self-sufficient through his religion, and the foremost is the one who is self-sufficient through his Lord. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who recites the Qur'an but does not act by it, the moderate is the one who recites the Qur'an and acts by it, and the foremost is the reciter of the Qur'an who acts by it and knows it. It was also said: the foremost is the one who enters the mosque before the muezzin's call to prayer (adhan), the moderate is the one who enters the mosque after the adhan has been called, and the wrongdoer is the one who enters the mosque when the prayer has already been established (iqamah), because he has wronged himself of the reward and has not obtained for himself what others obtained. Some people of knowledge said regarding this: rather, the foremost is the one who attains both the time and the congregation, and thus attains both virtues; the moderate is the one who, if the congregation is missed, does not neglect the time; and the wrongdoer is the one heedless of the prayer until both the time and the congregation are missed, so he is more deserving of the designation of wrongdoing. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who loves himself, the moderate is the one who loves his religion, and the foremost is the one who loves his Lord. It was also said: the wrongdoer is the one who takes his due but does not give what is due, the moderate is the one who takes his due and gives what is due, and the foremost is the one who gives what is due and does not take his due.

A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The foremost is the one who embraced Islam before the Hijrah, the moderate is the one who embraced Islam after the Hijrah, and the wrongdoer is the one who did not embrace Islam except under the sword, and all of them are forgiven. I say: al-Tha'labi mentioned these views and more in his Tafsir. In sum, they are two extremes and a middle, and the moderate (al-muqtasid) is the one who holds firmly to the course (al-qasd), which is the avoidance of inclination. From this is the saying of Jabir ibn Hunayy al-Tha'labi:

*We grant the kings peace as long as they keep to the course with us,*
*and killing them is not forbidden to us.*

That is, we offer them reconciliation as long as they ride the course with us, that is, as long as they do not oppress; and killing them is not forbidden to us if they transgress. Therefore the moderate holds a station between the two stations: he is above the one who wrongs himself and below the one who is foremost in good deeds.

﴿That is the great bounty﴾ means Our bringing them the Book. It was also said: that choosing, with Our knowledge of their faults, is the great bounty. It was also said: the promise of Paradise to these three categories is a great bounty.

**The third:** People have discussed placing the wrongdoer before the moderate and the foremost. It was said: mention first does not imply honour, as in His saying: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal﴾ [al-Hashr: 20]. It was also said: the wrongdoer is placed first because of the abundance of sinners among them and their dominance, while the moderate are few in comparison to them, and the foremost are fewer than the few. This was mentioned by al-Zamakhshari, and no one else mentioned it. It was also said: the wrongdoer is placed first to emphasise hope on his behalf, since he has nothing to rely upon except the mercy of his Lord; the moderate relies on his good opinion, and the foremost relies on his obedience. It was also said: the wrongdoer is placed first so that he does not despair of the mercy of Allah, and the foremost is placed last so that he does not become conceited by his deed. Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sadiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The wrongdoer is placed first to inform that one can only draw near to Him through the bestowal of His mercy and generosity, and that wrongdoing does not affect the choosing when there is care from Him. Then He mentions the moderate in the second place, because they are between fear and hope. Then He concludes with the foremost, so that no one feels secure from the plotting of Allah. And all of them are in Paradise through the sanctity of the word of sincerity: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi said: He gathered them in the choosing, removing the causes from the giving, because choosing necessitates inheritance, not inheritance necessitating choosing. For this reason it is said in the wisdom literature: "Correct the lineage, then claim the inheritance." It was also said: He placed the foremost last so that they would be nearer to the gardens and the reward, just as He placed the monasteries and churches before the mosques in Surah al-Hajj, so that the monasteries would be nearer to destruction and ruin, and the mosques nearer to the remembrance of Allah. It was also said: when kings wish to join things in mention, they put the nearer first, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in retribution, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-A'raf: 167], and His saying: ﴿He bestows female offspring on whom He wills and bestows males on whom He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 49], and His saying: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal﴾ [al-Hashr: 20]. I say: How well has the one said who said:

And the ultimate of this generosity is you, but it [only] reaches the ends at the last of matters.

Fourth issue: His saying, "Gardens of Eden they will enter" (*jannatu 'adnin yadkhulunaha*). He grouped them together in the entering because it is an inheritance, and the disobedient and the dutiful are equal in an inheritance when they both acknowledge the lineage. So the disobedient and the obedient are both joined to the Lord.

It was also read as *"Jannatu 'adnin"* in the singular, as if it were a garden specific to the foremost (*al-sabiqun*) because of their fewness, as has been mentioned previously. And *"Jannati 'adnin"* in the accusative is by an implied verb (*idmar*) that the apparent verb explains, meaning: they enter the gardens of Eden, they enter them. This applies to all of them, and it is the correct view, God willing, Exalted is He.

Abu 'Amr read *yudkhaluna-ha* with a *damma* on the *ya'* and a *fatha* on the *kha'*, and he said it is based on His saying, "They will be adorned [therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein is silk]" [[See vol. 12, p. 28.]].

"And they will say, 'Praise be to God, who has removed from us all grief.'" Abu Thabit said: A man entered the mosque and said, "O God, have mercy on my estrangement, console my loneliness, and facilitate for me a righteous companion." Abu al-Darda' said: "If you are truthful, then I am happier with that than you are. I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants; of them is one who wrongs himself, and of them is one who is moderate, and of them is one who is foremost in good deeds'" [Qur'an 35:32] — he said: "This foremost one comes and enters Paradise without reckoning; as for the moderate one, he is reckoned with an easy reckoning; and as for the one who wrongs himself, he is detained in the place of standing, rebuked and reproached, and then he enters Paradise. They are the ones who say, 'Praise be to God, who has removed from us all grief; indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative'" [Qur'an 35:34].

In another wording: "As for those who wronged themselves, they will be detained for a long time on the Day of Gathering, and then it is they whom God meets with His mercy. They are the ones who say, 'Praise be to God, who has removed from us all grief; indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative,' up to His saying, 'and no fatigue will touch us therein'" [Qur'an 35:35].

It was also said: "He is the one who is taken to account in his station," meaning that he is expiated for what afflicts him of distress and grief. From this is His saying: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ [Qur'an 4:123], meaning in this world. Al-Tha'labi said: "This interpretation is more fitting to the apparent meaning, because He said, 'Gardens of Eden they will enter,' and because of His saying, 'those whom We chose from among Our servants,' and the disbeliever and the hypocrite were not chosen."

I say: This is the correct view. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The likeness of the hypocrite who recites the Qur'an is like the sweet basil: its scent is pleasant, but its taste is bitter." So he informed that the hypocrite recites it, while the Exalted and Glorified God informed that the hypocrite is in the lowest depth of the Fire. Many disbelievers, Jews, and Christians also recite it in our time.

Malik said: "Someone who has no good in him may recite the Qur'an."

*Al-nasab*: fatigue. *Al-lughub*: exhaustion.

The verse, "As for those who disbelieve, theirs is the Fire of Hell" (﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهُمْ نارُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾). When Allah mentioned the people of Paradise, their states and their speech, He mentioned the people of the Fire, their states and their speech.

("It shall not be decreed for them so that they die") like His words: ﴿They will neither die therein nor live﴾ [al-A'la 13][[see vol. 1 p. 227]].

("Nor shall its punishment be lightened for them") like His words: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment﴾ [al-Nisa' 56][[see vol. 5 p. 253]].

("Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one") that is, every disbeliever in Allah and His Messenger. Al-Hasan read (فَيَمُوتُونَ) with a nun. In that case the negation has no answer clause, and (فَيَمُوتُونَ) is coordinated with (يُقْضى), the sense being: "It shall not be decreed for them, and they shall not die," like His words: (﴿and they will not be given leave, so that they may make excuses﴾) [[see vol. 19 p. 164]]. Al-Kisa'i said: "(﴿and they will not be given leave, so that they may make excuses﴾) is written with a nun in the Mushaf because it is the end of a verse, whereas (لَا يُقْضى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا) is not the end of a verse." Each of the two may take whatever is permissible in the other.

("And they will cry out therein") that is, they will call for help in the Fire with a loud voice. Al-Sukhrukh is a loud voice; al-sarikh is one who seeks help, and al-musrikh is one who gives help. He said:

"Whenever a terrified crier came to us,
the shout was like the clanging of the zanabib."
[The poem is by Salamah ibn Jandal. Al-zanabib (plural of zunbub) is a nail that is found on the socket of a spearhead.]

("Our Lord, bring us out") that is, they say: "Our Lord, bring us out of Hell and return us to the world."

("We shall do righteous deeds") Ibn 'Abbas said: "We shall say: there is no god but Allah." This is the meaning of their words: (﴿other than what we used to do﴾), that is, of shirk. That is: we shall believe instead of disbelieving, obey instead of disobeying, and comply with the command of the Messengers.

("Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed?") This is the answer to their plea, that is, it will be said to them. So the saying is implied. Al-Bukhari gave the chapter heading: "Chapter: Whoever reaches sixty years, Allah has left him no excuse regarding his lifespan, because of the words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed, and the warner came to you?' This refers to gray hair." He narrated to us: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Mutahhar said: Umar ibn 'Ali narrated to us, he said: Ma'n ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah has left no excuse for a man whose term He delayed until he reached sixty years."

Al-Khattabi said: "A'dhara ilayhi" means he brought him to the furthest limit of excuse. From this comes their saying: "One who has warned has cleared himself," that is, he has established his own excuse by presenting his warning. The meaning is that whoever Allah has granted a lifespan of sixty years has no excuse left, because sixty is close to the battlefield of deaths. It is the age of turning back in repentance, humility, awaiting death and meeting Allah the Exalted. Thus there is an excuse upon an excuse: the first through the Prophet (ﷺ), and the two deaths [al-mawtan (with the mim vowelled with a damma or fatha and the waw sukun): death] at forty and at sixty.

'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Hurayrah said, interpreting His words "Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed": it is sixty years. It has also been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said in his admonition: "Indeed, whoever is given early warning has been given a thorough excuse. A caller will call from Allah, the Exalted, to the sons of sixty: 'Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed, and the warner came to you?'" It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it is forty years, and from al-Hasan al-Basri and Masruq the same. Malik said: "I met the people of knowledge in our city, and they sought both the world and knowledge and mixed with people, until one of them reached forty years. It was also said that it is the Messenger; this was said by Zayd ibn 'Ali and Ibn Zayd. Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sufyan, Waki', al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, al-Farra' and al-Tabari said: it is gray hair. It was also said: the warner is fever. It was said: the death of relatives and kin. It was said: the perfection of the intellect. And "nadhir" here means "indhar" (warning).

I say: gray hair, fever and the death of one's family are all warnings of death. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Fever is the forerunner of death." Al-Azhari said: its meaning is that fever is the messenger of death, that is, it is as if it signals its arrival and warns of its coming. Gray hair is also a warner, because it comes in the age of middle years, and it is a sign of leaving the age of youth, which is the age of play and sport. He said:

"I saw gray hair as one of death's warnings to its owner,
and that is enough warning for you."

Another said:

"I said to her: gray hair is the warner of my life,
and I am not blackening the face of the warner."

As for the death of family, relatives, companions and brothers, it is a warning of departure at every time and moment, every hour and every age. He said:

"I see you carrying them, and you cannot turn them back,
so it is as if you will soon be carried and not returned."

Another said:

"Death at every moment spreads the shroud,
while we are heedless of what is intended for us."

As for the perfection of the intellect, by it the realities of matters are known and good deeds are distinguished from bad, so the intelligent person works for his Hereafter and desires what is with his Lord, and so he is a warner. Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 40:

(Nay, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion) meaning: vain things that deceive, which is the saying of the leaders to the lowly: "These deities will benefit you and bring you near (to Allah)." The Qur'anic statement of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they should cease [to exist]﴾. Nothing comes into existence except by His bringing it into being, and nothing remains except by His preserving it.

The "in" (inna) here is in a position of nasb (accusative), meaning "lest" (karahata an tazula, "out of aversion to their ceasing"), or "so that they do not cease" (li'allā tazula). Alternatively, it may be understood according to its sense, since the meaning is that Allah prevents the heavens and the earth from ceasing. On this reading there is no need for an implied element. This is the view of al-Zajjaj (Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj, a grammarian).

﴿And if they were to cease, none could hold them after Him﴾. Al-Farra' (Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra', a grammarian) said: that is, even if they were to cease, none would hold them. Here "in" means "ma" (not). He said: this is like His saying: ﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turn yellow, they would indeed continue to disbelieve after it﴾ (al-Rum 30:51) [see p. 45 of this part]. It is related from Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i) that he said: a man from the companions of Ibn Mas'ud entered upon Ka'b al-Ahbar (Ka'b ibn Mati' al-Ahbar, a Jewish convert to Islam) to learn knowledge from him. When he returned, Ibn Mas'ud said to him: "What did you gain from Ka'b?" He said: "I heard Ka'b say: the sky revolves on a pivot like the pivot of a millstone, on a pillar upon the shoulder of an angel." Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) said to him: "I wish you had turned over with your mount and its saddle! Ka'b has lied. He has not even abandoned his Judaism! It is also related from Ibn Abbas something similar, and that he said to a man arriving from Syria: "Whom did you meet there?" He said: "Ka'b." He said: "What did you hear him say?" Then He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Forbearing, Forgiving﴾, because the meaning, as some of the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have stated, is: Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease because of the disbelief of the disbelievers and their saying that Allah has taken a son.

Al-Kalbi said: when the Jews said "Uzayr is the son of Allah" and the Christians said "the Messiah is the son of Allah," the heavens and the earth almost ceased from their places, so Allah restrained them and revealed this verse concerning it. His words, may He be exalted: ﴿They swore by God, with their most solemn oaths, that if a warner came to them﴾. They were the Quraysh. They swore this before God sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), when news reached them that the People of the Book had denied their messengers, and so they cursed whoever among them had denied his prophet. They swore by God, may His name be exalted, (*if a warner came to them*), meaning a prophet, (*they would surely be better guided than any one of the nations*), meaning among those who denied the messengers from the People of the Book. The Arabs used to wish that a messenger would come from among them, as messengers had come from the Children of Israel. When there came to them what they had wished for, namely a warner from among themselves, they recoiled from him and did not believe in him.

(*Out of arrogance*), meaning out of obstinacy in refusing faith. (*And the evil plotting*), meaning the plotting of evil deeds, which is disbelief, and deceiving the weak, and turning them away from faith so that their followers would multiply. The feminine form in *"min ihdal-umam"* (*than any one of the nations*) agrees with the feminine *ummah* (nation), as al-Akhfash said.

Hamzah and al-Akhfash read *"wa-makra s-sayyi'"* and *"wa-la yahiqu al-makru s-sayyi'u"*, dropping the i'rab (the inflectional vowel marking that shows a word's grammatical case) in the first and keeping it in the second. Al-Zajjaj said: this is a lahn (a grammatical error), and it became a lahn because he dropped the i'rab from it. Al-Mubarrad claimed that this is not permissible in speech or in poetry, because the vowels of i'rab may not be dropped, since they were introduced to distinguish between meanings. Some grammarians found it too great a thing that al-A'mash, despite his eminence and standing, should read this way. They said: he would only pause on it, and whoever transmitted from him made a mistake. They said: the evidence for this is that it is a complete utterance, and that the second word, since it was not a complete utterance, was given i'rab by consensus; and the vowel in the second is heavier than in the first, because it is a *damma* between two *kasras*.

Some grammarians cited in support of Hamzah this saying of Sibawayh, in which he and others recited:

*When they become crooked, I say: "Companion, straighten them!"*
*With the desert, like the sailing ships in motion.*

*Al-dau*: the desert. *Amthal al-sufun*: loaded mounts that cross the desert as ships cross the sea.

And another said:

*So today I drink, not one who gains sin,*
*A sin from God, nor an uninvited drinker.*

This verse is by Imru' al-Qays. *Mustahqib*: one who acquires sin that bears him along. *Al-wa'il*: one who enters upon a people who are drinking without being invited. He said this when his father was killed, and he vowed not to drink wine until he avenged him. When he took his vengeance, drinking became lawful for him, in his view, and he would not sin by drinking it, since he had fulfilled his vow.

But this offers no proof, because Sibawayh did not permit it; he only related it from some grammarians. A report that is attributed to some scholars does not constitute proof, and how much less when it came in an irregular manner and out of the necessity of poetry, and it has been disputed.

Al-Zajjaj claimed that Abu al-Abbas recited:

*When they become crooked, I say: "Companion, straighten them!"*

and that he recited:

*So today drink, not one who gains sin*

with the alif of the imperative treated as a connecting alif. Al-Nahhas mentioned all of this.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Hamzah read *"wa-makra s-sayyi'"* with the hamzah vowelless, because he found the vowels heavy. Perhaps he cut the vowel short and it was taken as a sukun, or he paused briefly and then began *"wa-la yahiqu"*.

Ibn Mas'ud read *"wa-makran sayyi'an"*.

Al-Mahdawi said: whoever made the hamzah in *"wa-makra s-sayyi'"* vowelless does so either on the basis of pausing on it, treating the connected reading as if it were a pause, or because he made the hamzah vowelless to avoid the succession of *kasras* and *ya's*, as in the verse:

*So today drink, not one who gains sin.*

Al-Qushayri said: Hamzah read *"wa-makra s-sayyi'"* with the hamzah vowelless, and some people considered this an error. Others said: perhaps he paused on it, because it is a complete utterance, and the narrator made a mistake and transmitted it in continuous recitation. The discussion of such cases has already preceded, and we said: whatever is established through wide transmission or mass transmission (tawatur) as having been recited by the Prophet (ﷺ) must be permissible, and it is not permissible to say that it is a lahn. Perhaps the intention of those who went so far as to call it wrong is that others are more eloquent than it, even though it is eloquent.

﴿And the evil plotting does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾, meaning the consequence of shirk does not befall anyone except those who committed shirk. It has been said that this is a reference to their being killed at Badr. The poet said:

*They pushed away death, and it departed from them by a cubit, after it had been about to encompass them.*

That is, to descend upon them. This is the view of Qutrub. Al-Kalbi said: *yahiq* means *yuhit* (encompasses). *Al-hawq* is encompassing; one says: *haqa bihi kadha*, meaning it encompassed him.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that Ka'b said to him: "I find in the Torah: 'Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Then I will show you this in the Quran." He asked: "Where?" He said: "Recite: *And the evil plotting does not encompass anyone except its own people.*" Among the proverbs of the Arabs is: "Whoever digs a well for his brother falls into it headfirst."

Al-Zuhri transmitted that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not plot, and do not help a plotter, for God, may He be exalted, says: *'And the evil plotting does not encompass anyone except its own people'*. Do not transgress, and do not help a transgressor, for God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Whoever breaks his oath, breaks it only to his own detriment﴾ [al-Fath: 10], and God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Your transgression is only against yourselves﴾ [Yunus: 23]." Some of the wise said:

*O you who are wrongdoing in your deed,*
*Injustice is returned upon the one who did it.*
*Until when will you, and until when,*
*Count the calamities and forget the blessings?*

In a hadith: "Plotting and deceit are in the Fire." His words "in the Fire" mean that in the Hereafter they will bring their practitioners into the Fire, because they are among the characteristics of the disbelievers, not of the righteous believers. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, said in the same context of this hadith: "Plotting, deceit and betrayal are not among the characteristics of the believer." In this there is the most forceful warning against adopting these blameworthy traits and departing from the noble character of faith.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So do they await anything but the way of the earlier peoples?﴾ meaning they are only awaiting the punishment that descended upon the earlier disbelievers.

﴿So you will not find any change in the way of God, and you will not find any alteration in the way of God﴾. Meaning, God has carried out punishment upon the disbelievers and made that a way (sunnah) concerning them, so He punishes whoever deserves it with its like. No one can change that, nor can anyone transfer the punishment from himself to another. *Al-sunnah* is the way, and its plural is *sunan*. This has already passed in Al 'Imran, and He attributed it to God, may He be mighty and majestic. In another place He said: *"The way of those whom We sent before you of Our messengers"*, and He attributed it to the people, because the matter concerns both sides. It is like the *ajal* (term), which is sometimes attributed to God and sometimes to people. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The term of God is surely coming﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 5], and He said: ﴿But when their term comes﴾ [al-Nahl: 61].

**The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 45:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If God were to call mankind to account for what they have earned﴾, meaning for their sins.

(﴿He would not leave upon its back a single creature﴾) Ibn Mas'ud said: He means all living creatures that crawl and move. Qatadah said: This happened in the time of Noah, peace be upon him. Al-Kalbi said: "a creature" means only jinn and humans, excluding others, because they are the ones charged with obligation through reason. Ibn Jarir, al-Akhfash and al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: By "creature" here he meant only humans, to the exclusion of others. I say: The first view is more apparent, because it comes from a great companion (sahabi, a Companion of the Prophet). Ibn Mas'ud said: The dung beetle nearly suffers punishment in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam. Yahya ibn Abi Kathir said: A man was enjoining good and forbidding evil, and another man said to him: "Look to yourself, for the wrongdoer harms only himself." Abu Hurayrah said: "You have lied! By God, other than whom there is no god, and then he said: By Him in whose hand my soul is, the bustard dies of starvation in its nest because of the wrongdoing of the wrongdoer." Al-Thumali and Yahya ibn Sallam said regarding this verse: God withholds the rain, so everything perishes. Something similar has been mentioned earlier in (surah) al-Baqarah, from Ikrimah and Mujahid, in the explanation of ﴿and those who curse curse them﴾ [[See vol. 2, p. 186, second edition.]]. They are the insects and beasts, which are afflicted by drought because of the sins of the evil scholars who conceal the truth, so they curse them. We also mentioned there the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, regarding His saying ﴿and those who curse curse them﴾: "(They are) the creatures of the earth."

(﴿But He defers them until a specified term﴾) Muqatil said: The specified term is what He promised them in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Yahya said: It is the Day of Resurrection.

(﴿Indeed God is ever Seeing of His servants﴾), that is, of those among them who deserve punishment. The word that governs "idha" (إِذَا) cannot be "basiran" (seeing), just as it is not permissible to say: "al-yawma inna Zaydan kharijun" (today, indeed Zayd is going out). Rather, the word that governs it is "ja'a" (came), because of its resemblance to the particles of conditionality, and the nouns that are used as conditionals are governed by what follows them. Sibawayh does not hold that "idha" is used as a conditional except in poetry, as the poet said:

"When our swords fall short, their connection
is our steps toward our enemies, and we strike."

[[The line is by Qays ibn al-Khatim al-Ansari. See vol. 1, p. 201, second or third edition.
"Vol. 15."]]

The surah of "Fatir" is concluded, and praise be to God.
